subject: Proposal: pulse-based first-token & sustained token/sec SLOs for streaming endpoints
messages:
From: Paul Reynolds <paul@blueharbor.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Streaming vs sync SLA — what can Redwood commit for interactive UI?

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're excited about Redwood's runtime performance, but before we scope the pilot we need to understand SLA guarantees for interactive use. Specifically:

- What time-to-first-token (TTFT) SLOs do you commit to for streaming endpoints for short prompts (<512 tokens)? We aim for sub-300ms first byte to keep perceived latency snappy.
- For sustained output, what tokens/second can you guarantee (and how do you measure that — P50/P95 over what window)? We anticipate heavy multi-user concurrency and would like predictable per-session throughput rather than best-effort burst.
- Are there documented carveouts for cold cache/warmup or rate-limited windows?
- If streaming can’t meet our requirement, can you propose a fallback to sync endpoints with different guarantees? Also include any capacity reservation process and credit/penalty language.

We'd like to get a written proposal we can take to procurement. Can you loop in product/solutions engineering so we get precise metric definitions?

Best,
Paul
Paul Reynolds
Head of Platform
Blue Harbor

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Streaming vs sync SLA — what can Redwood commit for interactive UI?

Hi Paul — great question and thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (product/runtime) and Marissa (solutions) to put numbers against these items. High level: we can draft a pilot SLO package that separates: 1) a "first-pulse" (first-token) latency SLO for low-latency interactive sessions and 2) a sustained-token-rate SLO for steady-state streaming across sessions.

Quick proposal (we'll refine in the doc and specify P50/P95 windows):
- First-pulse (for prompts <= 512 tokens): target P50 = 120ms, P95 = 260ms when served from warmed routing and KV cache; a 500ms upper bound for occasional cold-starts.
- Sustained token throughput: baseline guaranteed 45 tokens/sec per session for the pilot; burst allowance to 120 tokens/sec for short 3s windows when capacity permits.
- Warm-up carveout: first 10 requests after model variant swap or cache eviction may be outside the P95; we'll call this a 60s "warm window" for the pilot.
- Fallback policy: automatic failover to sync endpoints if streaming node pool is saturated; sync endpoints carry a different SLO (complete-response within Xs) and lower per-token unit costs.

I've attached a one-page draft that defines the metrics and the capacity request we'll need from your side (pilot-sla-draft.pdf). Marissa — can you validate the customer impact language and the revenue/contract ask? Karthik — can you confirm whether the 45 tok/s baseline is realistic on the Dedicated pool without additional quantization?

Next steps: I can schedule a short call with our engineering team to walk through the warm-up behavior and the failure modes. If we can agree, we'll produce a pilot SLO and an accompanying capacity matrix for procurement.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Streaming vs sync SLA — what can Redwood commit for interactive UI?

Stephanie / Marissa — quick technical clarifications and a suggested measurable definition to avoid ambiguity in procurement:

Suggested metric names & definitions (for the SLA doc):
- first_token_latency_ms.P50 and .P95 — measured from request arrival at ingress to emission of the first token at the client-facing edge. Exclude customer-side network latency; measured over 1-minute rolling windows, aggregated over the billing day.
- sustained_token_rate.tokens_per_sec.P50/P95 — per-session sustained emission rate measured over 30s sliding windows; guarantee applies when requests are routed to Dedicated pilot pool.
- burst_window.seconds — define a short-term allowance (we recommend 3s) where per-session emission can exceed the baseline guaranteed rate up to the configured burst cap.
- warmup_exemption — a 60s window after a model variant change or cold cache eviction where first_token_latency may not meet P95. This must be documented and limited per rollout event.

Operational notes:
- KV cache warm-up is the dominant cause of first-token variability for long-context models; recommend the pilot include a pre-warm step in the mutual action plan.
- For guaranteed sustained rates, we need a Dedicated (reserved) pool with pinned capacity per customer; shared hosted pools can't provide per-session guarantees at scale without reservations.
- Quantization impacts throughput; 16-bit fp vs int8 variants change the burst profile. If Blue Harbor requires the 120 tok/s burst reliably, we should plan for an int8-optimized variant and validate quality regressions with their eval set.

Cost/contract recommendation: reserve a small dedicated pool for the pilot (see capacity-matrix.xlsx). If procurement wants financial credits for missed SLOs, suggest a capped credit model tied to P95 miss counts rather than open-ended penalties.

Happy to join the call.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer, Director, Product — Runtime

Paul — thanks for the patience while we pulled the team together.

Summary of the pilot proposal attached (pilot-sla-draft.pdf) and the recommended capacity reservation (capacity-matrix.xlsx). Key bullets for your procurement/ops team:

- Measured SLOs: first-pulse (first_token_latency_ms) P50=120ms / P95=260ms; sustained_token_rate baseline = 45 tok/s per session (P95), burst to 120 tok/s allowed for 3s windows.
- Warm-up carveout: 60s after model variant swaps or cache eviction. We'll include a pre-warm step in the mutual action plan to minimize this window.
- Requirements from Blue Harbor: sign the pilot reservation (short term Dedicated pool), provide a representative eval set to validate int8 quantized variant if you want the 120 tok/s burst.
- Remediation: if P95 misses exceed the threshold in a billing month, we'll issue a standardized credit (defined in the draft) tied to the missed P95 events.
